# Preface {.unnumbered}

**Arisbe** is an environment for *doing logic in pictures, not pictures of logic* — Charles
Sanders Peirce's "moving pictures of thought" made operational, with Frithjof Dau's
formalization as the guarantor of correctness.

The central engineering and research problem the system exists to solve is the **inerrant
correspondence between an existential graph's linear written form and its graphical drawn
form** — picture and proposition denoting the same mathematical object across every
transformation, every layout, every edit, every round-trip. That contract is the book's
spine; it gets its own chapter in Part I and is treated in depth in Part IV.

## How this book is organized

The book follows the [Diátaxis](https://diataxis.fr) shape so that one source can serve both
a linear read and task-oriented lookup:

- **I · Why** — what Arisbe is, the central problem, and the philosophy underneath it.
- **II · Getting started** — install and run it from the repository, draw your first graph,
  find the door that fits your background, and (for scholars) read the research invitation.
- **III · Using Arisbe** — the three modes in practice, the worked examples, and
  import/export including the Peirce-edition publishing path.
- **IV · How it works** — the architecture, the correspondence contract in depth, and a map
  of what is built.
- **V · Reference** — linear formats, the core API, the glossary, and prior art.

## One source, two renders

This book is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from the project's own documentation. The
same source renders to:

- a **browseable web help** (an HTML site, also served in-app — see *Install & run*), and
- a **book** (PDF and epub).

The reader chapters are the canonical docs that live under `docs/`, selected and ordered here;
the project's design-of-record, roadmap, and session notes stay in the repository and are
deliberately excluded from the reader's book.

> **New here?** Jump to **II · Getting started → Install & run**, then **Your first graph**.
